report:
No episode in K14–K18 (Sanjac_Rec_91) meets the question. I recorded 9 candidate moments, all near misses (grade 0), so there are no grade 2 or grade 1 episodes and no window grades to submit. All 9 records were accepted with no rejects, and `label get` shows them stored.

The main problem across these chunks is that the robot drives at about 2.0 m/s and constantly weaves, so a person's sideways drift in the image mostly comes from the robot's own motion. I tracked each person in the lidar scans and removed the robot's movement by hand. The helper script for that (`track.py` in the job's tmp folder) wasn't permitted to run.

| Chunk | Moment | Grade | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| K14 | K14-a, 8.0–9.2 s: person in the road on the right | 0 | Standing still looking at a phone; moved only about 0.17 m while the robot drove 1.6 m, so not an oncoming walker |
| K14 | K14-b, 14.4–16.0 s: oncoming group on the left | 0 | Walks a straight line; sideways offset stays at about 1.3 m. The 14.8 s dip in the robot's forward-path distance is a ground arc in the scan, not a person |
| K15 | K15-a, 42.0–44.0 s: two people by the right barrier | 0 | Standing or walking away from the robot, not oncoming; the crowd ahead stays out of passing range |
| K16 | K16-a, 72.0–73.6 s: man in white, passes left | 0 | Straight approach; offset 2.2 → 2.1 m |
| K16 | K16-b, 75.6–77.3 s: woman in navy, passes left | 0 | Straight approach at about 0.8 m/s; offset steady at about 1.8 m. The 77.36 s dip to 0.59 m is a ground-strike artifact in the scan |
| K16 | K16-c, 77.5–79.3 s: couple, passes close on the right | 0 | Offset −1.41 → −1.46 m while the robot's heading barely changes |
| K17 | K17-a, 104.2–105.5 s: man in orange cap on the left curb | 0 | Same body direction and walking line across the native frames; his drift in the image comes from the robot's 10° right turn. The couple ahead is walking away |
| K18 | K18-a, 117.3–119.5 s: man in orange shirt, nearly head-on, passes close on the left | 0 | Closest call. The robot's speed (~2.0 m/s flat) and heading (5.7° excursion) would pass, but his path is a steady ~6° diagonal with only 0.2 m total sideways drift, within the tracking error |
| K18 | K18-b, 121.5–124.0 s: oncoming couple, passes left | 0 | The robot turns 20° during the encounter (+0.8° to −19.2°), over the 15° limit |

Two verdicts are less certain than the rest:
- **K17-a:** the lidar can't cleanly separate him from the crowd on the left sidewalk, so that verdict rests mainly on the camera frames.
- **K18-a:** marked FALSE because there's no distinct course change. It's the one moment worth a second look if you want to probe the boundary.

This isn't a comparison question, so no pairs apply.
